_meta.indication: OLINVYK is an opioid agonist indicated in adults for the management of acute pain severe enough to require an intravenous opioid analgesic and for whom alternative treatments are inadequate.
_meta.receipt_date: Original NDA submitted November 2, 2017; Complete Response resubmission submitted February 7, 2020 (Submission Date).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (morphine-comparator) study; patients randomized 1:1:1:1 to three oliceridine PCA regimens, placebo, or morphine, with a 48-hour treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate-to-severe acute pain following bunionectomy (nonvisceral/hard-tissue pain model), pain intensity NRS ≥ 4.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's prespecified primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients who responded to study medication vs. placebo at the 48-hour NRS assessment (responder defined by ≥30% SPID improvement and other criteria); FDA based efficacy conclusions on the SPID over 48 hours (SPID48).
pivotal_trials.result: In FDA's SPID48 analysis, all three oliceridine doses (0.1, 0.35, 0.5 mg) showed statistically greater pain reduction than placebo (estimated mean difference vs placebo 46.4, 53.1, and 78.7, respectively; all p<0.01); morphine (difference 107.6) was superior to all three oliceridine doses.

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Oliceridine (TRV130) for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Acute Pain After Bunionectomy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (morphine-comparator) study; patients randomized 1:1:1:1 to three oliceridine PCA regimens, placebo, or morphine, with a 24-hour treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate-to-severe acute pain following abdominoplasty (visceral/soft-tissue pain model), pain intensity NRS ≥ 5.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's prespecified primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of responders vs. placebo at the 24-hour NRS assessment; FDA based efficacy conclusions on the SPID over 24 hours (SPID24).
pivotal_trials.result: In FDA's SPID24 analysis, two of the three oliceridine doses were superior to placebo: 0.35 mg (mean difference vs placebo 14.9; p=0.017) and 0.5 mg (19.2; p<0.01), while the 0.1 mg dose (2.0; p=0.75) was not; morphine difference was 28.1.

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Oliceridine (TRV130) for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Acute Pain After Abdominoplasty

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, constipation, pruritus, and hypoxia. In bunionectomy (Study 1), for the placebo and 0.5 mg arms respectively, nausea was 24% vs 63% and vomiting was 6% vs 41%. Serious risks include life-threatening respiratory depression and QT prolongation with daily doses exceeding 27 mg.
target_moa: Oliceridine is a full opioid agonist relatively selective for the mu-opioid receptor; it is a G protein-biased ligand that binds the mu-opioid receptor and stimulates G protein-coupling with reduced beta-arrestin 2 recruitment. Its principal therapeutic action is analgesia.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for addiction, abuse, and misuse; life-threatening respiratory depression; neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome; and risks from concomitant use with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was held in October 2018 during the first review cycle; concerns expressed included insufficient safety data and QT prolongation.

summary.text: Oliceridine was a 505(b)(1) new molecular entity with Fast Track designation (granted December 2, 2015). Two breakthrough therapy designation requests were denied, and priority review was not granted (standard review). The original NDA (submitted November 2, 2017) received a Complete Response on November 2, 2018 following an October 2018 Advisory Committee meeting; the applicant resubmitted on February 7, 2020, leading to approval, with deferred pediatric studies required under PREA.

citations.quote: The original application received a Complete Response (CR) action on November 2, 2018, because of clinical, nonclinical, and product quality deficiencies.

Since the applicant was initially proposing a total daily dosage of 40 mg, one major clinical deficiency from the first submission was inadequate safety data to support the proposed maximum daily dosage.
